end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown to home.
Identified that longer journeys can use more fuel and may need cooling, increasing electricity use.
Compared Assam tea, Himachal apples, and nearby bananas using travel distance.
Practised links between food miles, fuel, pollution, freshness, and cooling.
Suggested local food as a way to reduce food miles; limits of this approach remained unclear.
end.parentNote: Asha practised defining food miles and tracing food from where it grows to the home, rather than counting only the shop journey. Rohan used distance to explain fuel use and connected cooling with extra electricity; they also corrected the idea that the source does not matter. They still mixed up imported food with being better or more nutritious, and this was not corrected by the last time it appeared. At home, compare two foods and discuss where each was grown, how far it travelled, and whether cooling or transport was needed.
